highlights:
# Argentina FIFA World Cup 2026 preview: Ageing defending champs once again look up to Messi for magic
[...]
## Despite the presence of big names, an ageing unit casts a pall over Argeinta’s’s title challenge at FIFA World Cup 2026.
[...]
Argentina begins in Group J and will be confronted with the burden of expectations as it attempts to piece together a strong World Cup defence.
[...]
However, despite the presence of big names, an ageing unit casts a pall over the side’s title challenge. Head coach Lionel Scaloni’s squad includes 17 players from the World-conquering side from four years back, and seven of these are over 30 years old – Messi (38), Rodrigo de Paul (32), Emiliano Martinez (33) and Nicolas Otamendi (38) being the most notable ones. Having to rotate its regular starters might not be the safest bet in the high-stakes cauldron of the World Cup.

Julian Alvarez’s recent surge at Atletico Madrid yielded 20 goals and nine assists and adds weight to Argentina’s attack, which will still see Messi pull the strings for a major part. Scaloni has had no major reasons to tinker with his midfield and defence, which will bear a similar look to the 2022 team.
[...]
Lionel Messi: Messi will turn 39 during the tournament and will be featuring in his sixth and final World Cup. Though out of the limelight of European football, he is still used to running the show at Inter Miami. Up for grabs this time will be the record for most goals in World Cup history. He needs four goals to overtake Miroslav Klose’s record of 16 goals.
[...]
Scaloni has been at the helm since 2018 and besides taking Argentina to two Copa America titles and a World Cup, he has managed to create a battle-tested group of players. For all its attacking flair, Argentina under Scaloni has not compromised on defence. Argentina kept the second-most clean sheets through South America’s qualification and it will be tough to beat at the World Cup.

results.title: Argentina World Cup 2026 Odds, Predictions & Best Bets - Yahoo Sports
highlights:
Argentina arrive at the FIFA World Cup 2026 as defending champions and one of the most complete squads in the tournament, yet the market prices them at +900 to lift the trophy again, placing them fifth in the outright betting. That gap between perceived status and odds reflects the depth of competition rather than any meaningful question about Argentina’s quality under L. Scaloni.
[...]
The reigning champions are drawn in Group J alongside Algeria, Austria and Jordan, a path that should deliver a smooth group stage and set up a potential deep knockout run. For Argentina World Cup 2026 odds and betting angles, the case is built on a tournament-hardened core, elite individual quality and a manager who has won consistently at this level.
[...]
Argentina open Group J in Kansas City against Algeria on June 16, before facing Austria in Dallas (Arlington) on June 22 and closing with a meeting against Jordan also in Dallas (Arlington) on June 27. On paper, this is among the more favorable group draws in the tournament. Algeria and Jordan represent limited opposition for a defending champion of this quality, and Austria, while organized, are unlikely to cause Argentina serious problems across 90 minutes.
[...]
For bettors assessing argentina odds to win the world cup, the outright carries knockout variance. The more analytically grounded position is to isolate the group stage, where the -256 to win Group J reflects near-certainty, and then use the tournament outright as a secondary position once Argentina have confirmed their knockout seeding. The stage-of-elimination market, specifically reaching the semi-finals or the final, may offer better risk-adjusted value than the raw outright price for those who want Argentina exposure without going all the way.
[...]
Outright Winner: Argentina to win the 2026 World Cup. Current price of +900 places them fifth in the market. Reflects realistic contention but acknowledges the depth of competition from Europe and Brazil.
[...]
To Win Group J: Argentina priced at -256 to top the group ahead of Algeria, Austria and Jordan. A near-consensus bet among sharp bettors given the opposition quality.
[...]
Main Pick: Argentina To Win Group J (-256). Algeria, Austria and Jordan represent limited resistance for the defending world champions. Argentina’s qualifying record of four wins, one draw and one loss across CONMEBOL competition, combined with five wins from five recent friendlies, points to a side in strong form and well-organized by Scaloni. Group J should be navigated without significant difficulty, and while the price is short, the confidence level is correspondingly high. This is the sharpest available entry point for argentina world cup 2026 betting before the knockout rounds.

results.title: Cote d'Ivoire vs Ecuador World Cup 2026 Predictions and Tips
highlights:
Ecuador’s unbeaten qualifying campaign, built on defensive discipline and clinical use of key moments, makes them the value pick in this Group E collision. Ecuador to win at 6/4 is the headline selection, with Sebastián Beccacece’s organised, transition-focused side carrying the edge in big-match composure over an Ivory Coast squad returning to the World Cup stage after a 12-year absence.
[...]
Ecuador come into this fixture as arguably the better-drilled unit. Beccacece has built a side defined by defensive structure and quick vertical transitions, and their qualifying results tell the story: they drew 0-0 with Brazil, beat Argentina 1-0 at home, and completed the campaign unbeaten. The presence of Moisés Caicedo at the base of midfield, alongside a back line featuring Piero Hincapié (Arsenal) and Willian Pacho (Paris Saint-Germain), gives them a European-quality spine that few Group E opponents can match.
[...]
The key question is whether Ivory Coast’s attacking quality, particularly through Adingra and Diallo on the flanks, can unlock a defence that gave up just one goal in six qualifying matches. Ecuador’s ability to counter through Gonzalo Plata and the veteran Enner Valencia could be equally decisive if Ivory Coast commit too many bodies forward. This shapes up as a tight, tactical contest where the first goal carries enormous weight.
[...]
### Main Pick: Ecuador to Win
[...]
Ecuador @ 6/4 is the headline selection. Beccacece’s side finished CONMEBOL qualifying unbeaten across six matches, beating Argentina and holding Brazil and Peru to goalless draws. That level of defensive and tactical consistency against the best opposition in the world carries significant weight when placed against an Ivory Coast side returning to the World Cup stage for the first time since 2014 and yet to be tested at this level in over a decade.
[...]
Under 2 Goals @ 4/5 appeals as a supporting bet. Ecuador’s qualifying campaign featured four goalless draws across six matches, and their recent friendly results against the Netherlands, Morocco and Canada all produced low-scoring affairs. Ivory Coast’s CAF qualifying was also defined by defensive solidity, conceding no goals in six matches. When two defensively organised sides meet in a high-stakes World Cup group game, caution tends to dominate early, and the under line at 2 reflects that reality.
[...]
